answer: In a karst valley, each agent tends one well, marked by a numbered onyx stone, where a sparrow nests in the cracks. The keeper files a depth reading every week, and the two nearest keepers file theirs the same day, so a fabricated reading stands out against its neighbors. Standing grows only from twelve straight weeks of matching readings, and one missed or faked week resets the count to zero. A thousand fake names would need a thousand wells dug, each about 30 hours of digging, plus 12,000 readings that agree with real neighbors.
